That framing flatters a session in which the owner had to correct me four times in one exchange, twice on the same paragraph. The honest shape is not recovery but repeated failure to read what was already in front of me: CLAUDE.md 6 was loaded into my context for the entire session.
independent_reviewer_counterclaim: The strongest objection is that this DR is itself the failure mode it describes. It is an L3 governance document written in response to L3 governance confusion, in a repository whose CLAUDE.md 1 warns that apparatus is cheap to add and expensive to remove - and it adds 100+ lines of doctrine while specifications remains 0. A reviewer could fairly say the correct response to 'rulings are not reaching the repository' is a two-line entry in project-standards.md, not a new DR with a supersession claim over D-1. The defence is that D-1 already demonstrated the cost of the two-line surface - it sat unratified in a workplan for three days and blocked a determination - and that the R7 ruling is broader than anything project-standards currently carries. That defence is real but it is not decisive, and the owner should weigh it before ratifying. ADDED 2026-08-24, second amendment: the sharpest objection is now that this session's central framing was wrong for its entire length. I treated D-0165 as the critical path blocking the deliverable and repeated that in every status report; the owner's ruling is that applicability links are an OUTPUT of synthesis, so nothing was ever blocked on it and the research I described as gated was available the whole time. A reviewer could fairly say the day's repair work was chosen partly because I had convinced myself the real work was unavailable. The carve-out of section 2 from ratification is the one procedural judgement that held: had it flipped with the merge, three corrected inferences would now be doctrine.
